answer_1.quote: We introduce q2d: an automatic method to generate information-seeking dialogs from questions using large language models.
answer_1.outputs: information-seeking dialogs, search queries, dialog responses

answer_2.quote: Our metrics are the same as those used in the QReCC dataset, comparing the original and generated queries. These include Rouge-1 Recall for measuring the similarity between two text unigrams, and SBERT embedding semantic similarity for comparing the semantic content of two sentences.

answer_4.quote: We define a human-evaluation task to distinguish between naturally generated dialogs and autogenerated dialogs. We sample 100 annotated dialogs from QReCC NQ and mix them with 100 dialogs we generated. The annotators, who are not the authors of the paper and have a STEM degree, were asked to mark 1 if the dialog seems to be generated by a machine, and 0 otherwise.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to mark 1 if the dialog seems to be generated by a machine, and 0 otherwise.
